title: Reference-Counted Sub-Allocator with Non-Tracing Collector in Chronos-Interpreter
topic: The garbage collector never looks for garbage
author: Mateus Yonathan
journal: Polyglot Systems Lab Agentic Research Preprints

abstract: Chronos-Interpreter's default garbage collector relies on tracing and cycle detection, which introduces nondeterministic pauses and complicates reasoning about memory usage. We propose a minimalistic collector that never scans for garbage; instead, it relies on explicit reference counting coupled with a global registry that tracks live objects. The design guarantees that each allocation is $O(1)$ and each deallocation is amortized $O(1)$ with occasional $O(log K)$ coalescing when the pool expands. We prove that the collector preserves a zero-double-free invariant and that the arena remains contiguous. Static analysis of the abstract syntax tree confirms that the implementation contains 150 SLOC and 14 function blocks, yielding a low structural complexity. The source code is publicly available at \url{https://github.com/myonathanlinkedin/Chronos-Interpreter-advanced-lab/tree/main/algorithms/20261105_150214_the_garbage_collector_never_lo}.
